caption:
Two landings. Two and a half years apart. Under 200 metres.

Surveyor 3 landed on the Moon in April 1967, a robot inside a small crater.
Apollo 12 came in November 1969. Its lander, Intrepid, touched down close by.
Astronaut Pete Conrad walked to the robot. Less than 200 metres, or 650 feet.

What the astronomers say: the APOD 3D picture is made from two photos taken from slightly different spots, like your two eyes.

NASA picture: JSC, S69-57076. Lunar Orbiter 3 photo of the Apollo 12 site.
